text:
Sarah L.: Quick question — where do folks think the circuit-breaker logic for smart routing should live? policy engine vs per-region sidecar?
Mike B.: leaning sidecar for fast local reaction, keeps policy engine simpler
Priya S.: agree on local reaction, but sidecars make global consistency harder (rotations, canaries)
Alex C.: tradeoff: sidecar = low-latency trips, central = consistent decisions + easier rollout
Sarah L.: main requirements: avoid cascades, respect tenant SLAs, observable decisions, and smooth rollouts for policy changes
Priya S.: also need deterministic fallback choices so telemetry and billing match across hosts
Mike B.: idea: hybrid: keep primary breaker in sidecar for immediate backoff, but central policy can assert longer-term disable/override
Alex C.: hybrid sounds reasonable. We need a clear API: sidecar exposes breaker state and accepts control messages from policy service
Sarah L.: suggestion for interface: `GET /v1/breaker/{route}` returns {state, cause, until_ts} and `POST /v1/breaker/override` for central ops
Priya S.: what about scale? Policy service should not chatty-poll sidecars. Use pub/sub: policy pushes override events, sidecars subscribe
Mike B.: +1. Use protobuf envelope with sequence numbers so sidecars can reconcile when reconnecting
Alex C.: concern: when central overrides, we need proof in traces (span tag) so we can correlate decisions and billing adjustments
Sarah L.: agree — include `policy_id` and `revision` in the state and emit an event for every change
Priya S.: failure modes: if policy service is partitioned, sidecars must degrade to local heuristics rather than wait for central commands
Mike B.: local heuristics should be simple: error-rate threshold, queued request depth, tail latency; keep identical math across regions
Alex C.: we should publish the heuristic formula in docs and make it config-driven so Dedicated/Private customers can tune it
Sarah L.: rollout plan: start with sidecar-only circuit-breaker for short windows, shadow central evaluator, then enable central override for a small percent of tenants
Priya S.: telemetry: record both local trips and central overrides separately. add tags: {source: local|central, policy_id: x} so alerts can target root cause
Mike B.: ops playbook: central override should include human-readable reason and TTL; short TTLs for automated overrides only
Alex C.: security: overrides must be signed and authenticated (mTLS) — we cannot allow a rogue push to disable protections
Sarah L.: sounds like consensus. Action items: 1) Priya to draft sidecar API + proto, 2) Mike to sketch local heuristic defaults, 3) Alex to add trace tags and telemetry schema, 4) Sarah to write rollout checklist
Priya S.: I'll put a draft in the RFC repo by EOD tomorrow :thumbsup:
DevOps Bot: Next deploy window scheduled at 2024-04-05 02:00 UTC for sidecar alpha
Mike B.: awesome — thanks team, will sync if blockers appear
